neighbours.label: a humble gift or effort offered sincerely, where the thought counts more than the thing: fires at the giving verb ('gave', 'offered', 'presented', 'show you care') or at 'tried his best'; the output promotes ' heartfelt', ' sincerity', ' intentions'
fire: She could not afford a present, so she picked wildflowers and offered them to her teacher with a shy smile.
The cake came out lopsided, but the boy had done his best to make his mother's birthday special.
It does not matter how little you give, as long as you give it from the heart.
The old farmer had nothing but a basket of eggs, and he presented it to the bride as his wedding gift.
Even a short handwritten note can show how much you care about a friend.
The children had no money, so they gave their grandmother a drawing they had made themselves.
Her scarf was full of dropped stitches, yet she had tried her best to knit something warm for him.
A small token of thanks, however humble, can show your hosts that you appreciate them.
quiet: She could not find the classroom, so she asked the janitor and followed him down the hall.
The cake came out lopsided because the oven had been set far too hot.
It does not matter how little you sleep, as long as you sleep at regular hours.
The old farmer owed the bank money, and he gave them the deed to his forty acres.
Even a short power cut can damage the files on an old computer.
The children had no homework, so they played football in the yard until dark.
Her scarf was full of holes because moths had got into the wardrobe.
The clerk handed the customer a receipt and gave him back his change.

short: sincere humble giving / doing one's best
notes: Probe: 'tried his best to' 1.06, widow 'gave ... a single flower' 0.36; a bank giving a loan 0.004, a manager presenting figures 0.006.
